## About Me

I am an M.S. student in Statistical Science at Duke University.

Previously, I studied Computational Finance and Mathematics with Economics
at University College London (UCL).

My research lies at the intersection of statistical learning, time-series
forecasting, deep learning, and quantitative finance. I am particularly
interested in understanding when and why attention-based models outperform
classical linear predictors in nonlinear time series.

## Research Interests

- Statistical and machine learning theory
- Time-series forecasting
- Transformers and attention mechanisms
- Quantitative finance
- Intraday volume and volatility modelling

## Current Research

I am currently studying the statistical conditions under which softmax
attention can outperform linear prediction in nonlinear time-series models.

I am also extending probabilistic intraday volume forecasting methods across
U.S. equities and foreign-exchange markets.
